title: Clay flatten_record: <column>_fields must never overwrite a real column
answers: Why is my Clay enrichment data missing in the warehouse table?
What does the _fields column in Clay synced tables mean?
Clay column name collides with _fields column
body:
clay/clay.py:flatten_record maps each Clay cell to a value: only `success` cells keep a value; error/pending/empty become None. Enrichment `fields` go to sibling `<column>_fields`.
Invariant: if the record already has a real column named `<column>_fields`, the real column wins and the enrichment metadata is dropped (guard `fields_column not in record`). Order-independent, so tests put `X_fields` first.
Also: clay has no primary key (primary_keys=None) and uses full replace; get_schemas sets supports_incremental=False and supports_append=False. Table IDs come from pasted text via parse_table_ids (regex `t_...`), since Clay has no list-tables endpoint.
applies: Clay source row flattening and schema config
